title: Cross-ministry coordination on problematic gaming among students
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how ministries coordinate on problematic gaming, which cuts across mental health, education, student welfare and youth development, and whether preventive policy has become a joint strategic priority.
response: MOE works with other agencies on students' mental well-being and digital media use, from Cyber Wellness lessons in schools to referrals to social service agencies or the National Addiction Management Service for assessment and treatment. It partnered MSF and the Health Promotion Board on Parenting for Wellness resources, and co-developed the Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media with the Ministry of Digital Development and Information and MSF. On regulation, the Code of Practice for Online Safety was introduced under the Broadcasting Act in 2022 for social media services, with measures extended to app distribution services in 2025. Asked whether MOE is the lead agency, Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi described a "many helping hands" approach, and said MOE does not currently engage gaming platforms directly on addictive design.

key_points.point: Cyber Wellness lessons run from primary to pre-university level and cover balancing online and offline activity.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MOE's Cyber Wellness lessons for primary to pre-university students teach the importance of maintaining a healthy balance of online and offline activities

key_points.point: Schools identify students with gaming concerns and refer them, with parental consent where required, to social service agencies for early intervention or to NAMS for assessment and treatment.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Schools identify students with gaming concerns and refer them, with parental consent where required, to social service agencies (SSAs) for early intervention

key_points.point: MOE partnered MSF and the Health Promotion Board on Parenting for Wellness resources for parents.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MOE has partnered the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Health Promotion Board to develop the Parenting for Wellness resources

key_points.point: The Positive Use Guide on Technology and Social Media was co-developed by MDDI, MOE and MSF and includes tips on limiting gaming.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: which includes practical tips on limiting gaming activities

key_points.point: The Code of Practice for Online Safety was promulgated by IMDA for social media services, with app distribution services added in 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: the introduction of the Code of Practice for Online Safety that was promulgated by the Infocomm Media Development Authority for social media services

key_points.point: MOE does not currently engage gaming platforms directly on making gaming less addictive; regulation is through the Broadcasting Act and the Code of Practice for Online Safety.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: we do not, at least currently, engage them directly as a Ministry

key_points.point: On whether MOE is the lead agency, the reply describes a "many helping hands" approach spanning society and the online space.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: it really takes a "many helping hands" approach because the issue spans quite broadly

key_points.point: The approach is calibrated by age: primary students learn safe online practices and respectful online relationships.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: at the primary levels, we nurture our students to learn good habits in terms of safe online practices and respectful online relationships

left_open: Whether MOE is the single lead agency with clear ownership and outcome accountability for problematic gaming.
Whether preventive policy has been formally designated a joint strategic priority across ministries.
supplementary: Whether MOE is the lead agency, and whether the Government engages gaming platforms on addictive design features.
